input.question: How come the F-35 program cost way more to develop than the F-22 despite being generally less technologically advanced?
input.ground_truth: F-35 is pretty much 3 different planes, that look similar. * Navy version has different wings and modifications to frame to support carrier landing. * Marine version has VSTOL. * Air Force version has better performance.

messages.content: You are a helpful AI assistant.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How come the F-35 program cost way more to develop than the F-22 despite being generally less technologically advanced?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, imagine you and your friend both want to build a really cool toy car. You decide to build yours by yourself, and your friend wants to build a toy car that *everyone* in your class can play with and that can change into different kinds of cars.

Your toy car is just for you, so you use simple parts and don’t worry too much if it breaks or if it looks a little weird. It doesn’t take as long or cost as much to make.

But your friend wants *everyone* to be able to play with their toy car, and they want it to turn into a race car, a truck, or even a helicopter! So your friend has to make sure the toy works perfectly for lots and lots of kids, in many different ways. They have to test it a *lot* to make sure it’s safe and doesn’t break. They also have to ask many grown-ups (like teachers and parents) what they think and make changes again and again. All of this takes a *lot* more time and money.

The F-35 is like your friend’s super toy car. Lots of countries want it, and it has to do many different jobs. The F-22 is like your toy car—just for one country and doesn’t have to change as much. So even though the F-35 isn’t *super* fancy in some ways, making it work for so many people and in so many ways makes it *way* more expensive to build than the F-22.
